subject: Post-demo pricing sensitivity & model traffic breakdown
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Eva Morales <eva@coralhealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo pricing sensitivity & model traffic breakdown

Thanks again for the demo time earlier, Eva — good discussion. Below is a concise recap of what we heard and a couple of practical pricing scenarios so you can see how different model mixes and token assumptions map to monthly spend. Please confirm or correct any assumptions so we can prepare a short pilot SOW.

Recap of requirements (what I captured)
- Primary use case: summarization + contextual retrieval for patient notes (high importance on accuracy + PII controls)
- Expected steady state: ~12k daily active users -> approx. 1.2M queries/month (your estimate)
- Typical request shape: 1) chat prompt + 2) system prompts + 2) reference docs pulled (we estimate ~750 tokens/request on average including responses)
- Peak: you called out a short daily burst tied to batch imports (~120-150 qps for ~20-40 minutes)

Key commercial scenarios (unit economics shown as $ / 1M tokens)
- Scenario A — conservative: $1,050 / 1M tokens (mix: 65% chat-large, 25% embeddings, 10% rerank)
  - Monthly spend @ 1.2M queries x 750 tokens ≈ 900M tokens -> ~$945 / month (math below)
- Scenario B — balanced (recommended): $800 / 1M tokens (mix: 55% chat-medium, 30% embeddings, 15% rerank)
  - Better at preserving latency and lowering cost with prefix caching + batching
- Scenario C — aggressive cost optimization: $600 / 1M tokens (mix: 40% chat-small/quant, 40% embeddings, 20% rerank)
  - Requires acceptance of slightly higher generation variance and small latency tradeoffs

Model mix assumptions (per your workload)
- Chat (chat-medium / chat-large variants): 55-65% of token volume for Q+A and summarization
- Embeddings (dense) for retrieval/semantic search: 25-35%
- Rerank / short scoring calls: 5-15% (low token but high QPS)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm a realistic monthly token target range (best guess / stretch)? your 1.2M requests/month * 750 tokens = ~900M tokens/month; if your internal analytics expect 2x that, call it out.
2) Do you have a hard budget target expressed as $ / 1M tokens or total monthly cap? you mentioned wanting sub-$700/1M if possible.
3) Procurement: who should I loop for contract/terms? (you mentioned procurement@coralhealth.io)
4) Compliance: need SOC2 + subprocessor docs? we can prepare a redacted SOC2 and data flow diagram for review.

Attached: coral_pricing_scenarios.xlsx (simple scenarios + token math), redwood_map.pdf (our recommended pilot instrumentation + KPIs)

If you prefer, I can sketch two pilot options: 3-week pilot capped at $10k with metrics collection, or a 6-week scoped evaluation with higher throughput to stress-test routing + cache hit assumptions. Suggest we lock decision-maker alignment and target KPIs in the next call.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Eva Morales <eva@coralhealth.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Coral Health Procurement <procurement@coralhealth.io>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing sensitivity & model traffic breakdown

Thanks Olga — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 12k daily users is conservative; our product team now expects 25k DAU in Q4 if onboarding goes well. That would push monthly queries to ~2.5M.
- Token estimate: 750 tokens/request looks plausible for summaries but can swing up to ~1,100 for long note syntheses.
- Budget: our procurement lead is aiming for ~ $600-$700 / 1M tokens target. We understand tradeoffs here; a tiered pricing model for the pilot would help.
- Pilot ask: yes to a 3–4 week pilot with instrumentation. We want a clear definition of success: recall/precision targets for summary quality + latency SLOs (95p < 600ms for chat responses if possible).

Looping in procurement now. Also copying our Product lead, Marco (marco@coralhealth.io), who will share a short sample of typical notes to help with token shape analysis.

—Eva
Head of Integrations, Coral Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Eva Morales <eva@coralhealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Coral Health Procurement <procurement@coralhealth.io>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing sensitivity & model traffic breakdown

Perfect — thanks for the details and for looping Marco. Quick response and proposed plan:

1) Pilot offer (3 weeks) — low risk
   - Capped spend: $10k total (we'll set hard caps in routing)
   - Instrumentation: request-level token telemetry, per-model latency breakdown, prefix cache hit rate
   - Deliverables: evaluation report with per-model cost, quality metrics (samples + evals), and recommended steady-state model mix

2) Pricing framing
   - We'll propose a tiered pilot price that targets $650 / 1M tokens for the pilot with explicit escalation steps if volume > 2M requests/month or tokens/month > 1.8B
   - If Coral wants an aggressive $600 / 1M target for production, we can put together a tradeoff doc showing model substitution + quantization impact on quality and expected latency delta

3) Next meeting: 30-min technical + procurement sync w/ Marco and procurement lead. Proposed times: Thu 10am PT or Fri 2pm PT. Which works best?

I uploaded a short starter SOW and the pricing scenarios to the HubSpot deal (link below). If procurement needs a redline, Ben can lead that thread.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/COR-2981
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X_example_redwood_poc_materials

Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — quick margin + model-cost ask (COR-2981)

Internal note — tagging for visibility.
Olga / Aisha, can you run a quick model-level unit-econ snapshot for the balanced pilot (650 / 1M target):
- Estimated served tokens by model (chat-medium, embeddings-dense, rerank-small) given the suggested 55/30/15 split and both 900M and 1.8B token scenarios
- Per-model expected infra cost (GPU-min + memory + kv-cache amortized) and expected list price -> margin at $650/1M
- Sensitivity table showing margin at $600, $700, $850 / 1M tokens

Also ask EngSRE to validate the peak burst handling with the KV cache assumptions — specifically: if cache hit = 40% during steady state, how does that change token redemption at peak?

Keeping this short; will pull the numbers into the commercial playbook once we have the snapshot.

—Ben
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
